help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Will you come to the party? – Yes, I'll be there.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Next week we will finish the project.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The subject is ihr, so werden becomes werdet; the infinitive verpassen goes to the end.
help.tips[0].en.text: Ich werde, du wirst, er wird, wir werden, ihr werdet, sie werden. Morgen | wird | es | regnen. Ich | werde | dich nie | vergessen.
help.tips[0].en.title: werden + infinitive at the end
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: On Saturday we're going to Hamburg.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: werden + infinitive is for promises, predictions and warnings: Ich werde dich nie vergessen. A plain plan stays in the present: Heute Abend gehe ich ins Kino.
help.tips[1].en.text: Prediction: Es wird bald kalt. Promise: Ich werde anrufen. Intention: Nächstes Jahr werde ich mehr lesen. Warning: Du wirst zu spät kommen! Plain plans stay in the present: Morgen gehe ich ins Kino.
help.tips[1].en.title: When to use it instead of the present
help.tips[1].en.trap: English needs 'will' for almost every future; German mostly doesn't. Overusing werden sounds like a weather forecast. Default to the present + time word.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The light is off – she's probably asleep.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: He is not answering the phone – he is probably still in the meeting.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: wird + wohl + infinitive is a guess about the present: he is probably ill.
help.tips[2].en.text: Er wird wohl im Büro sein. Sie werden schon zu Hause sein. This is not the future at all — it's a guess about the present.
help.tips[2].en.title: werden + wohl = probably (now)
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: It's getting cold. — It's being built. — It will rain.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: She is becoming a doctor. — She is being operated on. — She will call tomorrow.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: werden + a noun means to become. The future needs an infinitive, the passive a participle.
help.tips[3].en.text: werden + adjective/noun = become (Er wird Arzt). werden + participle = passive (Es wird gebaut). werden + infinitive = future (Es wird regnen). Look at what follows.
help.tips[3].en.title: werden has three hats
help.context.en: What will you do next year? – I'll start an apprenticeship and do more sport. And I promise: I'll call you every week. – You'll surely forget that! – No, I won't forget. By the way: it'll rain tomorrow, take an umbrella.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: The infinitive is the last word.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: wollen means 'to want'; the future is werden.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: werden takes the infinitive, not a conjugated verb.
help.hookEn: Promises, predictions and good guesses: werden + infinitive says what will happen, and what is probably happening right now.
help.introEn: German usually talks about the future in the present tense with a time word — Morgen fahre ich nach Köln. The Futur I, werden + infinitive, is used when you want to stress that something will happen: a prediction (Es wird regnen), a promise (Ich werde dich nie vergessen), a firm intention (Ich werde ab Montag joggen), a warning (Du wirst dich erkälten!) — and, surprisingly often, a guess about the present (Er wird wohl krank sein = he's probably ill). werden conjugates like the passive helper you already know (werde, wirst, wird, werden, werdet, werden), sits in position 2, and pushes the infinitive to the end. In a weil- or dass-clause the order flips: …, dass es morgen regnen wird. Everyday speech prefers the present, but you need to understand both ways of talking about tomorrow.
help.rememberEn[0]: werden at 2, infinitive last; present + time word for ordinary plans.
sentences[0].whyEn: Futur I = werden + infinitive at the end: es wird … regnen.
sentences[1].whyEn: ich werde — a promise in the future tense.
sentences[2].whyEn: du wirst — werden changes its vowel: wirst, not werdest.
sentences[3].whyEn: wir werden — plural, same as the infinitive.
sentences[5].whyEn: er/sie/es wird — with i, the irregular singular form.
sentences[6].whyEn: ihr werdet — the ihr ending -t on werde-.
sentences[8].whyEn: ich werde … aufstehen — the separable verb stays whole as an infinitive.
sentences[9].whyEn: er wird — singular with the vowel change.
sentences[10].whyEn: wir werden — the future tense as a promise.
sentences[12].whyEn: es wird … schneien — a forecast, the future tense's main job.
sentences[13].whyEn: du wirst — encouragement in the future tense.
sentences[14].whyEn: Bald fills position 1, wird keeps second place.
sentences[15].whyEn: wird + wohl = assumption: he's probably ill — the future of guessing.
sentences[16].whyEn: ihr werdet — with bestimmt, a confident prediction.
sentences[17].whyEn: du wirst — the question about the future.
